title: Philadelphia's Academy of Natural Sciences Museum Closes as Supporters Seek Reopening
summary:
A favorite place for Philadelphia families has closed its doors. The Academy of Natural Sciences Museum closed on September 30, 2026, after families crowded in for final visits.

The museum opened to the public in 1828. Its dinosaur skeleton displays have drawn children since 1868. Visitors could also explore animal displays, meet live animals and learn from museum educators.

Drexel University has been responsible for the Academy's finances since 2011. The university said costs rose and attendance fell after the pandemic. During the museum's last weeks, however, attendance jumped.

Supporters organized marches, rallies and a petition with more than 114,000 signatures. Former museum worker Isa Betancourt returned to Philadelphia to help the campaign.

Before the closing date, the William Penn Foundation offered one year of temporary funding. That would give people time to explore longer-lasting solutions. Drexel said it was considering working with the foundation, but reopening would need a plan for paying costs over time.

The Academy holds more than 19 million scientific specimens, or samples used for study. Drexel says students and researchers will keep access to the collection. Public access remains unclear.

Philadelphia's city council also plans public hearings to learn why the museum closed and what could help it reopen.
why_it_matters: The closure affects a place where families learned about nature. Its future public access and a plan for reopening remain uncertain.
